### Contributing guidelines

- [x] I have read [CONTRIBUTING.md](https://github.com/echasnovski/mini.nvim/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md)
- [x] I have read [CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md](https://github.com/echasnovski/mini.nvim/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md)
- [x] I have updated 'mini.nvim' to latest version of the `main` branch

### Module(s)

mini.doc

### Neovim version

0.10.x

### Description

I have noticed that `mini.doc` by default adds ...(dots) between name and the link, like:
```
Table of Contents
  Setup..................................................|gopher.nvim-setup()|
  Install dependencies..............................|gopher.nvim-install-deps|
```

Which breaks default treesitter parser and [`conceal`](https://github.com/neovim/neovim/blob/f4d9a2983a49c1729f78ffbf6b1e6dcc30215d0d/runtime/ftplugin/help.vim) for help files.

---
I have played around with the code, and this seems to delete all dots from the Table of Contents.


```diff
diff --git i/lua/mini/doc.lua w/lua/mini/doc.lua
index bd47efd..839cae4 100644
--- i/lua/mini/doc.lua
+++ w/lua/mini/doc.lua
@@ -1024,7 +1024,7 @@ H.toc_insert = function(s)
       -- Use tag reference instead of tag enclosure
       local right = vim.trim((tag_section[i] or ''):gsub('%*', '|'))
       -- Add visual line only at first entry (while not adding trailing space)
-      local filler = i == 1 and '.' or (right == '' and '' or ' ')
+      local filler = i == 1 and ' ' or (right == '' and '' or ' ')
       -- Make padding of 2 spaces at both left and right
       local n_filler = math.max(74 - H.visual_text_width(left) - H.visual_text_width(right), 3)
       table.insert(lines, ('  %s%s%s'):format(left, filler:rep(n_filler), right))
```

### Reproduction

1. Create a directory for reproduction
1. Inside the created directory, create file init.lua and populate it with the following content:
```lua
local function root(p)
	local f = debug.getinfo(1, "S").source:sub(2)
	return vim.fn.fnamemodify(f, ":p:h:h") .. "/" .. (p or "")
end

local function install_plug(plugin)
	local name = plugin:match(".*/(.*)")
	local package_root = root(".tests/site/pack/deps/start/")
	if not vim.uv.fs_stat(package_root .. name) then
		print("Installing " .. plugin)
		vim.system({
			"git",
			"clone",
			"--depth=1",
			"https://github.com/" .. plugin .. ".git",
			package_root .. "/" .. name,
		}):wait()
	end
end

install_plug("echasnovski/mini.doc")

vim.env.XDG_CONFIG_HOME = root(".tests/config")
vim.env.XDG_DATA_HOME = root(".tests/data")
vim.env.XDG_STATE_HOME = root(".tests/state")
vim.env.XDG_CACHE_HOME = root(".tests/cache")

vim.cmd([[set runtimepath=$VIMRUNTIME]])
vim.opt.runtimepath:append(root())
vim.opt.packpath = { root(".tests/site") }

local minidoc = require("mini.doc")
minidoc.setup()

local hooks = vim.deepcopy(minidoc.default_hooks)
hooks.write_pre = function(lines)
	-- Remove first two lines with `======` and `------` delimiters to comply
	-- with `:h local-additions` template
	table.remove(lines, 1)
	table.remove(lines, 1)
	return lines
end

MiniDoc.generate({ "test.lua" }, "doc/gopher.nvim.txt", { hooks = hooks })
```
1. Inside the created directory create file `test.lua` and populate it with the following content:
```lua
--- *gopher.nvim* Enhance your golang experience
---
--- MIT License Copyright (c) 2025 Oleksandr Smirnov
---
--- ==============================================================================
---
--- gopher.nvim is a minimalistic plugin for Go development in Neovim written in Lua.
--- It's not an LSP tool, the main goal of this plugin is add go tooling support in Neovim.
---
--- Table of Contents
---@toc

---@toc_entry Setup
---@tag gopher.nvim-setup()
---@text Setup function. This method simply merges default config with opts table.
--- You can read more about configuration at |gopher.nvim-config|
--- Calling this function is optional, if you ok with default settings.
--- See |gopher.nvim.config-defaults|
---
---@usage >lua
---  require("gopher").setup {} -- use default config or replace {} with your own
--- <
---@param user_config gopher.Config See |gopher.nvim-config|

---@toc_entry Install dependencies
---@tag gopher.nvim-install-deps
---@text Gopher.nvim implements most of its features using third-party tools.
--- To install these tools, you can run `:GoInstallDeps` command
--- or call `require("gopher").install_deps()` if you want to use lua api.
--- By default dependencies will be installed asynchronously,
--- to install them synchronously pass `{sync = true}` as an argument.
```
1. Inside the created folder, run following command
```bash
nvim --noplugin --headless -u ./init.lua +qa
```

comment_data.body:
Thanks for the issue!

I can reproduce. The issue here is that dots do not create extra space in between entry name and its tag. This only breaks concealing characters, though, as the navigation part of the tag still works. Weirdly, I've been aware of this issue since #264 (since I don't use `@toc` in 'mini.nvim' itself), but didn't realize that.

I'll take a look.
This should now be resolved on latest `main` with adding extra pads between left and right parts for a better conceal. Thanks again for noticing!

title: mini.doc: adds too much dots in TOC which interferes help file parsing
